messages:
alex: Quick design idea: swap per-prefix monotonic counters for an "epoch-bucketed" eviction token map + a tiny probabilistic demote tag. Goal: cut per-prefix bytes and make cross-slab fairness easier. Sketch below.

julia: high level - how does this differ from the prefix token / lease hedging we've used? are we trading deterministic correctness for lower memory?

alex: We keep determinism for correctness-heavy ops (handoffs, writes) by consulting full lease. For eviction/admission we use a compact summary: (epoch_bucket, token_hash16, demote_prob4). It's intentionally lossy: token_hash16 is not unique but cheap.

sam: Concern: if token_hash16 collides aggressively we'll amplify eviction oscillation for small tenants. Any backoff plan?

alex: plan: collision mitigation layered with tenant-weighted grace. if we see repeated eviction churn for a tenant, we raise their local grace window and temporarily treat the compact summary as lower-confidence for N minutes.

leo: How do we handle deletes / re-creates (same prefix id but new owner)? epoch_bucket solves part of it?
alex: yes: epoch_bucket is advanced on full-delete/rename. We only require monotonicity within an epoch_bucket; cross-bucket we treat compact summaries as no-longer authoritative and force full-lease checks on next handback.

julia: Example layout?
alex: ```
// 6 bytes per prefix (packed)
// epoch_bucket: 24 bits, token_hash: 16 bits, demote_prob: 8 bits (0-255 => 0-100% quantized), flags: 8 bits
struct BucketedToken { u32_epoch_low24; u16_hash; u8_demote; u8_flags }
```

sam: Nice tight packing. What are the heuristics for demote_prob? E.g. hot prefix gets 0, cold gets 255?
alex: demote_prob is a hint: admission/ejection path uses it to bias selection. concrete mapping: recent accesses => lower prob; low access rate or read-only => higher prob. We use exponential decay counters sampled by reservoir to avoid per-prefix counters.

leo: Observability plan? we need to detect when lossy summary changes user-visible behavior.
alex: metrics: summary_hit_ratio (how often eviction/admit used summary vs full lease), collision_signal_rate (cases where token_hash mismatch caused fallback), eviction_churn_by_tenant, grace_window_triggers. dashboards per-tenant-p50/p95.
julia: Can we A/B by tenant size? small tenants may accept slightly higher churn if it saves memory. big tenants get stricter mode.
alex: yes - config rule: tenants with > X tokens get full-lease consult, mid-size get canary-lift, small get summary-first.

ops-bot: deploy-plan: feature-flag epoch-bucketed-summary set to canary=5% on cluster "cachepool-a" (requested by alex).

sam: rollout knobs: 1) global summary-threshold, 2) collision-backoff-time (default 5m), 3) emergency-force-full=true kill switch. Also add a sanity-check job that picks N random prefixes daily and compares summary decisions vs full-lease decisions.

julia: One more thought: make the token_hash derivation include a per-node salt so collisions are spread and diagnosable. store salt version in node metadata so we can rotate without breaking everything.
alex: agreed. next steps: write RFC w/ correctness proof sketch + canary metric gates + API for grace window control. I'll prototype in branch `evict/epoch-buckets` and open a PR for review. thanks all :rocket:
